title: For 45 contact binaries with strong TESS 2018-2026 period curvature, earlier ASAS-SN and SuperWASP timings show about 40 percent of the predicted offset; 403 systems show no V1309 Sco-like decay
abstract: Question: do the orbital-period changes that TESS measures in contact binaries continue as a constant dP/dt in earlier, independent data, and does any system show a fast, steady decrease like the merger progenitor V1309 Sco? Approach: we measured per-sector eclipse-timing shifts with a Fourier light-curve template for 749 contact binaries of the Prsa et al. (2022) TESS catalog (P = 0.2-1.0 d, 5,001 SPOC 2-min light curves, 2018-2026). We fit linear and quadratic ephemerides (403 vetted binaries). Then we measured season timings with the same templates in ASAS-SN (2012-2025) and SuperWASP (2004-2008) data and tested the TESS ephemerides backwards in time. Results: 118 of 403 binaries have a TESS quadratic term at 5 sigma or more (68 increases, 50 decreases; median |dP/dt| 0.068 s/yr). For strongly curved binaries, the observed earlier offset is a median 0.42 of the TESS-quadratic prediction about 4 years before TESS (45 binaries) and 0.34 about 12 years before (22 binaries); a constant dP/dt gives 1. The decade-mean dP/dt between the survey epoch and TESS is a median 0.35 of the TESS-window value. Apart from one rejected spot or blend case, no binary has a significant decrease faster than 0.44 s/yr, more than 100 times slower than V1309 Sco before its merger. Conclusion: most TESS-window period changes of contact binaries are parts of longer, non-secular variations. Limitations: timings are defined only modulo P/2, an empirical -274 s ASAS-SN time offset and a 98 s systematic term were applied, SuperWASP placement across 2008-2014 uses a trapezoid rule, and no cyclic models were fitted.

display.caption: O-C diagrams relative to the TESS linear ephemeris for eight contact binaries: TESS sectors (black), ASAS-SN V (orange) and g (blue) seasons, SuperWASP seasons (green), and the TESS-only quadratic ephemeris extrapolated backwards (violet). In the top row the TESS curvature continues; in the bottom row it does not.

(a) kappa, the observed fraction of the offset that the TESS quadratic ephemeris predicts for earlier survey seasons, against years before TESS. A constant dP/dt gives 1. (b) Decade-mean dP/dt from pre-TESS surveys to TESS against the TESS-window dP/dt (symmetric log axes); the violet line is 1:1.

Distribution of |dP/dt| in the TESS window for 403 vetted contact binaries: significant increases (blue), significant decreases (orange outline) and 3-sigma limits for the others (dashed). The pink band is the rate range of the Galactic-bulge merger candidates of Hong et al. (2024); the red line is V1309 Sco before its merger.

citations.reason: We use its copy of the Prsa et al. (2022) TESS eclipsing-binary catalog and its TESS bulk-download recipe; it studies detached binaries, and this work studies contact binaries.
Prsa et al. 2022, TESS eclipsing-binary catalog: target list, periods and epochs.
Latkovic et al. 2021 W UMa compilation: published long-baseline dP/dt for the aggregate literature comparison.
Hong et al. 2024, bulge contact binaries with decreasing periods: our result shows that dP/dt over a few years is often not secular, which is relevant to merger-candidate selection.
Tylenda et al. 2011, V1309 Sco: reference rate of a pre-merger period decrease.
